title: ProviderRequest
description: The provider-neutral input to a BrainProvider (ADR-0009). TurnExecutor builds one of these; each adapter translates it at the edge into Anthropic messages, an OpenAI-shaped payload, or an Ollama request. Nothing above the adapter ever constructs a vendor-shaped body.

breaking_changes: 1.1.0 (ADR-0039): cancellation_token_id now constrains to cancellation.schema.json's ULID pattern rather than accepting any string, including the empty one. Nothing in the repository produces a ProviderRequest yet, so nothing migrates.
compatibility.notes: `cancellation_token_id` is REQUIRED, not optional. ADR-0025 is explicit that optional cancellation is cancellation some call sites will omit, and those are exactly the ones that hang during barge-in. Adding a `role` value is MAJOR: adapters map roles onto vendor-specific message types and an unmapped role would be silently dropped, producing a request that looks fine and is missing context.

system.description: System prompt. Assembled by ContextAssembler; adapters place it wherever their vendor expects.

tools.description: ToolSpec IR. The adapter translates to native format. Tools the Policy Engine would deny for this turn's trust level SHOULD be filtered out here rather than offered and refused — offering a tool the model cannot use wastes tokens and invites a confusing refusal.

response_schema.description: Structured-output request. Adapters whose provider lacks native support fall back to prompt-based constraint plus validate-and-retry, and MUST report that via ProviderCapabilities rather than silently degrading.

cancellation_token_id.description: ADR-0025. Non-optional. ADR-0039: constrained to the same ULID pattern cancellation.schema.json pins token_id to, so the 200 ms cancellation clause has something to look the token up by.

trust_level.description: Effective turn trust, passed so the adapter can annotate untrusted spans in the prompt. Defence in depth only — the real control is the Policy Engine at dispatch, never the prompt.

ref.description: For image_ref: a URI or content-addressed handle. NEVER inline base64 — ADR-0006 keeps binary off this path, and a base64 image in a prompt log is a privacy problem as well as a size one.

examples.system: You are L.I.O.N.E.L, a local assistant. Answer in the language the user spoke.
